Manager’s Office, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

MAY 14, 2019

CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

MAYOR MITCHELL reported that she attended the SCAG General Assembly at which the new
officers were installed.

COUNCILMEMBER HUFF reported that she and COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN attended
the South Bay Housing Forum hosted by Senator Ben Allen where a variety of housing related
matters were discussed.

COUNCILMEMBER HUFF noted that she received an email from the League of California Cities
requesting that the City send a letter of opposition to SB 50 (Weiner). City Manager Prichard
noted that under current policy, the Mayor and City Manager can review the matter and
determine if a letter should be sent.

COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported that the City of Redondo Beach is working with
other cities to begin the process of preparing a State constitutional amendment to preserve local
control over housing and land use.

COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN also noted that he attended a teleconference where
Measure W funding allocation was discussed. He also noted that it was mentioned that cites
may want to consider forming stormwater utilities.

COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported that he and Senior Planner Naughton attended the
County Sustainability Conference which was very well presented and well attended. He noted
also that there is a national group of mayors, including several local mayors working
collaboratively on climate change issues.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ reported that she attended the West Vector Control Board
meeting noting that mosquito numbers in our area are lower so far this year. She expressed the
importance of being diligent in eliminating standing water due to the aedes mosquito. She also
noted that there are ticks in Los Angeles County that have tested positive for Lyme disease and
urged hikers and walkers on trails to check for ticks.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 14, 2019
 MAYOR MITCHELL provided a recap of the discussions from last week’s Regional Law
Enforcement Committee meeting regarding the status of the joint emergency preparedness
coordinator position, the joint emergency preparedness committee and the PVPUSD school
resource officer. She noted that that City staff will be finalizing the details on the joint position
and the school resource officer and bringing the matters back to each City Council for discussion
and consideration.

MAYOR MITCHELL reported that she and COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN attended a meeting
with PVPUSD and the City of Rancho Palos Verdes regarding pool use and the City’s summer
swim program and staff will be finalizing the MOU for continued use of the facilities.

MAYOR MITCHELL noted that she attended the dedication of Peninsula Seniors new location
in the City’s commercial center near the library. She suggested everyone stop by and visit the
new location.

MAYOR MITCHELL expressed appreciation to Supervisor Hahn for her efforts in convincing the
Metro Board to allocate Measure M funds to support SBCCOG’s regional broadband program.

MAYOR MITCHELL reported that today, the Board of Supervisors approved a $25,000 reward
for information leading to the apprehension and conviction of the person responsible for the
murder of Susan Leeds who was found dead in her vehicle in the parking structure at the
Promenade on the Peninsula in May of last year. She expressed appreciation to Supervisor
Hanh and the Board of Supervisors for this action.
